summary: Bradford treats public safety as a top mayoral priority, framing it around three themes: crime, congestion, and cost of living (DYHvvjDNgrj, DWFOTgOCdsC). Bradford consistently supports expanded police resources, including hiring 1,000 new front-line officers, placing officers in every TTC subway station, and creating Bail Compliance Units (DbJBNmfxr8V, DVhJtcuD2D5, CrO78kSgWyV). Bradford advocates bubble/safe access zones around places of worship, schools, and daycares to address antisemitism and hate crimes, culminating in the 2025 by-law's passage (DJ-VovGNcWT, DLqIg7XSd8J). Bradford opposes encampments near playgrounds, schools, and daycares and pushed 48-hour removal motions (DRAJ0bKguJx, DQ1p-5ECq1K). Bradford supports mandatory treatment for severe drug addiction, jet ski no-go zones at Woodbine Beach, enforcement against illegally modified e-bikes/mini-motorcycles, and criticizes Mayor Chow for insufficient action on TTC safety, encampments, and antisemitism (DcM1pudtgck, DMipr7MyKc4, DYnsJ1INHm5).

key_positions.stance: Supports increasing police staffing, including hiring 1,000 new front-line officers and placing uniformed officers at every TTC subway station.

Supports bubble/safe access zones (50m+ buffers) around places of worship, schools, and daycares to protect against hate and harassment, and worked with Councillor Pasternak for over a year to pass this by-law.
Opposes encampments, particularly near playgrounds, schools, and daycares, and supports 48-hour removal within 200 metres of these sites.
Opposes antisemitism and hate crimes, framing them as a public safety crisis requiring stronger enforcement and city-wide action.
Supports establishing no-go zones for jet skis at Woodbine Beach and stronger regulation, licensing, and enforcement for motorized watercraft.
Supports mandatory treatment for severe drug addiction, expanded recovery beds, and faster access to treatment.
Supports stronger regulation and enforcement against illegally modified e-bikes and mini-motorcycles, including bylaw updates, licensing, and police impoundment authority.
Supports Vision Zero road safety measures including speed cameras, speed limit reductions, school safety zones, and traffic calming installations.
Opposes Mayor Chow's approach to public safety, arguing she accepts crime and disorder as the cost of big-city life.
Supports the mayor sitting on the Toronto Police Services Board as the public official responsible for public safety.
